Quanzhou Jinjiang International Airport (IATA: JJN, ICAO: ZSQZ) is a dual-use military and commercial airport serving the city of Quanzhou in East China's Fujian province. It is located 12 km (7.5 mi) south of the city center (aka Licheng and Fengze Districts), in the county-level city of Jinjiang, which is under the administration of the prefecture-level city of Quanzhou. results.content:
Jinjiang (晋江; Tsìn-kang in Minnan, Jìnjiāng in Mandarin) is a mainly industrial city just across the river from Quanzhou in Fujian. Administratively, it is a county-level city in Quanzhou Prefecture, but for practical purposes it can be thought of as a suburb of Quanzhou. Population was a bit over two million as of the 2020 census.

results.title: Chinese Ancestry Research | **“The Really Useful China Maps”** | Facebook
results.content:
overseas Chinese descendants may have spent decades searching for their elusive ancestral hometown called ‘Chincan, Imperio de Chino’ without ever realizing the place they seek is… Jinjiang 晉江. [...] And perhaps that is why the name Jinjiang 晉江 feels strangely fitting after all.

For from the collapse of one empire came the great southward migration that helped shape Fujian itself, and centuries later, from poverty and migration came another rebirth across the seas. Again and again, the people scattered. Again and again, they rebuilt. Again and again, they rose — like a phoenix emerging not from desert flames or imperial fire, but from the currents of history itself. [...] And it is here that the story of Jinjiang 晉江 truly begins.

According to longstanding local tradition preserved in historical gazetteers and regional records, many of these displaced migrants eventually settled along a river in southern Fujian. The memory of the fallen Jìn 晉 court remained so deeply embedded within these émigré communities that the river itself gradually became known as the “Jìn River” 晉江 — the River of Jìn.
